sentences: Polynomial calculus derives contradictions through polynomial equations, with degree and total proof size measuring different resources.
The source asks whether a small-size proof can be converted into a small-degree proof without a large increase in size.
Reducing degree may force many additional intermediate equations even when low-degree refutations exist.
Understanding this tradeoff would determine whether separate upper bounds can be achieved by one useful proof.
The extraction omits the named systems and quantitative conversion target, so it does not establish a universal size-preserving degree-reduction conjecture.
